reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review contract, resource assessment rubric, fresh-review framework, the ResearchDefinition resource context, the full StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate, and the direct behavior findings whose `affectedResources` include `ResearchDefinition`. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were considered only as background context, as required. I also checked the local R4/R6 package evidence for same-name resource presence and the likely Evidence/EvidenceVariable migration shape.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `ResearchDefinition` was trial-use/FMM 0, so the standards-stability burden for preserving its wire model is weak. That makes removal or replacement more defensible than it would be for mature infrastructure or clinical workflow resources, but it does not eliminate the need for explicit migration guidance because PICO semantics can affect evidence and recommendation logic.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 removes `ResearchDefinition`, so R4 users need a resource-replacement migration; low FMM makes the removal defensible, but official mapping and endpoint/search transition guidance still matter.

reasoning.thesisMd: `ResearchDefinition` is not a mostly stable resource with a few local field breaks. The same-name R6 StructureDefinition is absent, `ResearchElementDefinition` is absent as well, and R6 lists these names as old types. Any R4 instance with `resourceType: ResearchDefinition` therefore fails before element-level compatibility can help.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a removed/replaced resource family. R4 `ResearchDefinition` centered on PICO-style links: mandatory `population`, optional `exposure`, optional `exposureAlternative`, optional `outcome`, and optional `library`, with the PICO roles largely mediated through `ResearchElementDefinition`. The closest R6 structures use `Evidence.variableDefinition` entries with required `variableRole` and `observed`/`intended` references to `Group` or `EvidenceVariable`. That is not a same-identity rename; implementers must choose a replacement representation and policy for comparator/alternative exposure semantics, referenced variable definitions, and formal library logic.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because the R6 base resource identity is gone, avoiding one more local element break has limited leverage unless the old resource family is retained. A full compatibility-preserving option would mean carrying deprecated `ResearchDefinition` and likely `ResearchElementDefinition` through R6, with validators, generated models, REST endpoints, search surfaces, and conformance metadata. For this FMM 0 trial-use artifact, that does not look like a clearly low-cost preservation step. The useful compatibility work is instead migration-program work: authoritative target guidance, ConceptMap/StructureMap material, and search/endpoint transition documentation.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The main less-breaking alternative is a transitional deprecated R6 `ResearchDefinition` plus `ResearchElementDefinition`. It would preserve many R4 instances but at the cost of parallel evidence-question models beside `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable`, including duplicate codegen, validation, REST, and search behavior. That is standards-review-worthy as a conscious tradeoff, but not a low-cost default. Lower-cost mitigations remain valuable: publish explicit mappings for population/exposure/exposureAlternative/outcome/library and identify recommended replacement endpoints and query patterns.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct HTTP and search findings are real runtime/API consequences for `ResearchDefinition`: clients can no longer discover or query a same-name endpoint in R6. They do not independently change the resource-level conclusion because they flow from the resource removal. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` operation and search changes, including `$meta`, `$validate`, `$convert`, and special search parameter metadata changes, are important platform issues but were not scored as `ResearchDefinition`-specific resource findings.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's main classification: major migration is already unavoidable, the shape is `removed-or-replaced-resource`, and resource-level migration dominates. The nuance is that `migration-program-dominates` should not be read as `nothing else matters`: the search/endpoint losses and missing official PICO mapping are still important transition items. I also agree that the possible less-breaking base design is only partial and not clearly low-cost for an FMM 0 resource.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the identity break and the need for a migration program. The main uncertainty is the official intended successor model, because the supplied inputs and local package evidence point toward `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable` but do not provide an authoritative ResearchDefinition-to-R6 ConceptMap or StructureMap.

findingConsiderations.title: ResearchDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive hard break. A valid R4 `ResearchDefinition` instance has no same-name R6 base StructureDefinition, generated model, ordinary REST resource type, or CapabilityStatement resource declaration. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable regardless of individual element-level changes.

findingConsiderations.title: ResearchDefinition's PICO content model has no lossless same-identity R6 mapping
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This explains why the migration is not just a resourceType string replacement. R4's role-specific PICO fields and `ResearchElementDefinition` references must be mapped into R6 evidence variable structures with policy choices for population, exposure, comparator/alternative exposure, outcome, and library logic. That is migration-program work even though it is downstream of the identity removal.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: For `ResearchDefinition`, the endpoint disappearance is a concrete API and conformance break, but it is derivative of the resource removal. Deprecated endpoint aliases or redirects could reduce client disruption only if an official successor representation is defined; otherwise the endpoint behavior must be solved as part of the broader replacement migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 clients using `ResearchDefinition` search cannot carry queries forward to a same-name R6 endpoint. This matters operationally, but the lower-cost fix is documented replacement search behavior tied to the chosen R6 model, not preserving old search parameters independently of the removed resource.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource` operation change can affect many resources, but under the review rules it is not scored as a `ResearchDefinition`-specific finding. It also has little additional leverage here because there is no R6 `ResearchDefinition` endpoint on which the operation would be preserved.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a platform-level `Resource`/`DomainResource` search metadata issue, not a ResearchDefinition resource-model change. It should be handled in shared behavior review rather than used to inflate the ResearchDefinition migration conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or confirm an authoritative R4-to-R6 migration map for `ResearchDefinition` and `ResearchElementDefinition`, especially for `population`, `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, `outcome`, and `library`.

Document replacement REST and search behavior for implementations that exposed R4 `ResearchDefinition` endpoints; consider deprecated aliases only where a clear successor endpoint exists and the server burden is acceptable.
Do not treat shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings as additional ResearchDefinition-specific break counts; route them through the shared behavior review track.

caveats: The review did not find an authoritative R6 ConceptMap or StructureMap for ResearchDefinition in the supplied local evidence.
The likely successor model is inferred from R6 `Evidence` and `EvidenceVariable`; a later official mapping could refine the migration details without changing the removed-resource conclusion.
